bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Relays the remote service's own result unchanged; it computes no number of its own, so the service is the authority for what comes back.
bio.jane/contract.question: Give me this accession's record from the archive named.

description: Fetch a sequence by accession from an authoritative archive (NCBI Nucleotide or Protein, ENA, UniProtKB, the iGEM Registry, Addgene, or the EBI Dbfetch gateway) and hand it downstream as a real record with its annotations. This is how a pipeline starts from a published sequence rather than from whatever happens to be open.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

accession.description: the accession to fetch, e.g. NC_005816, U49845, P38398, BBa_R0040. An NCBI accession may carry a window: `NC_005816 REGION: 5000..7000`.

db.description: Dbfetch only: which of its databases. Only applies when source is dbfetch.

format.description: Dbfetch only: which of that database's formats. Only applies when source is dbfetch.

record_index.description: which record to emit when the fetched file holds several (0-based).

source.description: which archive holds it. Values: ncbi (NCBI Nucleotide), ncbi-protein (NCBI Protein), ena (ENA), uniprot (UniProtKB), igem (iGEM Registry), addgene (Addgene), dbfetch (EBI Dbfetch).

name: fetch_record

circular.description: whether the archive says it is circular

featureCount.description: how many annotations came with it

length.description: its length in bases (or residues, for a protein)

name.description: the record name the archive gave it

provenance.description: the archive, the accession, the URL and when it was fetched — what makes the result re-fetchable

record.description: the fetched sequence, ready for a downstream node's $subject
